title: WTO | Services - negotiations
content:
WTO members continue discussions on advancing negotiations to achieve a higher level of market opening, as mandated in Article XIX of the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS). These talks began in 2000 under the original mandate contained in the GATS and became part of the Doha Round at the 2001 Doha Ministerial Conference. In 2011, members agreed on a waiver allowing preferential treatment to be granted to services and service suppliers of least-developed countries.
Negotiations of specific commitments, under Article XIX of the GATS,  take place in the Special Session of the Council for Trade in Services. The  current chair of these negotiations is Ambassador Zhanar Aitzhanova (Kazakhstan).  More recently, members have discussed proposals in the context of exploratory  discussions on improving market access commitments in services.
Members are also negotiating rules on domestic regulation in services,  in line with Article VI of the GATS, with the aim of ensuring that measures  relating to qualification requirements, technical standards and licensing  requirements do not constitute unnecessary barriers to trade in services.

KEY MILESTONES IN THE NEGOTIATIONS
Guidelines and the Procedures for the Negotiations on Trade in Services are adopted
Doha Development Agenda is adopted
Deadline for receiving initial offers
July Package establishes deadline of May 2005 for submission of revised offers
Hong Kong Ministerial Conference sets out detailed guidance on process and substance of services negotiations
Doha Round negotiations suspended
Resumption of Doha negotiations
Services Signalling Conference held as part of July 2008 package. Ministers exchange signals on improvements that could be expected in services.
Slowdown in negotiations overall due to failure to conclude agriculture and NAMA modalities
Ministerial Conference adopts a waiver to permit WTO members to grant preferential treatment to services and service suppliers from LDCs.
At the Nairobi Ministerial Conference, ministers acknowledge that members have different views on how to address the future of the Doha Round negotiations but note the strong commitment of all members to advance negotiations on the remaining Doha issues, including services. Some members say that new approaches are necessary.
Joint Initiative on Services Domestic Regulation
Under the Joint Initiative on Services Domestic Regulation,
WTO members are conducting negotiations, with the aim of developing disciplines to facilitate services trade. Participation in this Joint Initiative is open to all WTO members.
